purpose: Valbenazine is used to treat tardive dyskinesia, which is a condition that causes uncontrollable, repetitive movements of the face, tongue, or other body parts. These movements often develop in people who have taken certain psychiatric medications for a long time. This medicine helps reduce those unwanted movements so daily life feels more comfortable.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called dopamine to send signals that control movement. In tardive dyskinesia, there is too much dopamine activity in certain areas, causing those uncontrolled movements. Valbenazine works by reducing the amount of dopamine released in those areas, which helps calm the abnormal movements down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include feeling sleepy or drowsy, tiredness, and an unsteady or wobbly feeling when walking. Some people may also notice a faster or irregular heartbeat, dry mouth, or blurred vision. These effects are usually mild but let your doctor or pharmacist know if they bother you.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious drowsiness, so be careful driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. It may cause irregular heart rhythms (QT prolongation), so tell your doctor if you have any heart conditions. It can also worsen depression or cause thoughts of suicide in some people, so contact your doctor right away if your mood changes. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Most people start with 40 mg taken by mouth once daily. After one week, your doctor will likely increase the dose to 80 mg once daily, which is the usual maintenance dose. It can be taken with or without food, and it is best to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
